sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 4.5% a year from $70.3 billion in FY2016 to $104.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F205], but the path was a step change, not a straight line.
Revenue jumped 19.8% in FY2020 to $93.6 billion [F5][D183] and another 13.3% in FY2021 to $106.0 billion [F6][D230], then fell in each of the last three years to $104.8 billion [F10][D416].
The FY2020 surge came from a 19.3% comparable sales increase [P51], and FY2025's decline reflected comparable sales down 2.6% on a 2.2% traffic drop [P14].
Operating income compounded at just 0.6% over the window [F207], and net income fell 9.4% in FY2025 to $3.71 billion [F44][D418].
Merchandise sales were 98.0% of revenue in FY2025 [D465] and fell 2.0%, a 2.0pp drag on total growth [D466][D467].
Food & beverage grew 1.3% in FY2025 and contributed 0.3pp [D507][D508], while apparel fell 4.7% for a 0.7pp drag [D564][D565] and household essentials fell 3.2% for 0.6pp [D514][D515].
Food & beverage's share of revenue rose from 19.6% in FY2017 to 23.0% in FY2025 [D484][D506], the clearest mix shift toward frequency categories.
Operating income fell 8.1% in FY2025 against a 1.7% revenue decline [D417][D416], so there was no operating leverage; SG&A fell 2.0% [D432] while cost of revenue fell 1.3% [D431].
Diluted EPS fell 8.2% in FY2025 [D420] against net income down 9.4% [D418], as the diluted share count fell 1.3% [D434].
Operating margin was 4.9% in FY2025 [F34], below the 5.6% window median [D590] and far from the 8.4% FY2021 high [D589], though above the 3.5% FY2022 low [D588].
The FY2025 margin fell 0.3pp [D429], with cost of revenue a 0.3pp drag [D440] as the gross margin rate slipped to 27.9% from 28.2% [P12].
SG&A was 20.6% of revenue, flat on FY2024, including a 0.6pp benefit from interchange fee settlements offset by 0.2pp of business transformation costs [P11].
The largest move was FY2022, when operating margin fell 4.9pp [D290] as cost of revenue was a 4.6pp drag [D301], driven by markdowns, excess inventory and supply-chain costs [P38].
Net margin of 3.5% [F54] sits close to operating margin of 4.9% [F34], with the 22.3% effective tax rate [D403] and $445 million interest expense [X66] the main below-the-line items.
Operating cash flow was $6.56 billion and free cash flow $2.84 billion in FY2025 [F84][F104], a 2.7% free-cash-flow margin [D401] below the 4.5% window median [D596].
Operating cash flow fell from $7.37 billion in FY2024 [F83] on lower net earnings and lower accounts payable leverage [P7].
Free cash flow covered net income 0.77 times in FY2025 [D405] against a 1.01 times window median [D599], and capex of $3.73 billion was 1.19 times D&A [F94][D406].
Capex rose 28.9% in FY2025 [D423] on increased investment in new stores and remodels [P5], and management guides to about $5 billion in FY2026 [P4].
Cash and investments were $10.1 billion against total debt of $14.4 billion in FY2025 [D408][D409], a net debt position of $4.30 billion [D410].
Net cash was -4.1% of revenue [D411], slightly below the retail peer median of -3.5% [D613] and at the 50th percentile of six peers [D612]; the current ratio was 0.94x [F184].
Buybacks plus dividends were $2.46 billion in FY2025 [D412], 86.8% of free cash flow [D413], with $408 million of repurchases [X126] and $2.05 billion of dividends [X136].
The diluted share count fell from 582.5 million in FY2016 to 455.6 million in FY2025 [X107][X116], supporting EPS growth of 6.3% against net income growth of 3.4% [F210][F208].
Revenue has declined three years running, from $109.1 billion in FY2022 to $104.8 billion in FY2025 [F7][F10][R1], with FY2025 comparable sales down 2.6% [P14].
The current ratio of 0.94x [F184][R2] is at the window median of 0.94x [D602], so the sub-1.0x reading reflects a normal working-capital-negative retail model rather than new stress.
The FY2022 burn coverage of 2.4 years [D276][R3] is stale, since free cash flow has been positive in every year since [F102][F103][F104].
Operating margin has fallen two years in a row, 0.4pp in total [F32][F33][F34][R4], and the FY2022 buyback figure was later restated to $2,646 million from $2,826 million [R5][X123].
Whether revenue stops falling: a FY2026 figure above $104.8 billion [F10] would reverse the three-year decline, while another drop confirms it.
Whether operating margin holds above the 5.6% window median [D590] or slips toward the 3.5% FY2022 low [D588], with the FY2026 10-K the place to check.
Whether capex lands near the guided $5 billion [P4], which against FY2025 free cash flow of $2.84 billion [F104] would pressure the 2.7% free-cash-flow margin [D401].
